next_step: Calibrate the observation clock and readout independently, then run a held-out multi-clock stress test on the same physical preparation. Compare endpoint probabilities and projected activity with the one-clock homogeneous fit and the shared-clock hierarchy.
allocation: One worker-unit for observation calibration; one for the multi-clock stress test and comparison.
decisive_observation: After calibration, does the shared-clock feasible set explain cross-clock outcomes that the one-clock fit misses, and does it narrow enough to distinguish mechanistic alternatives?
outcome_decisions: If the shared-clock set explains the mismatch and narrows, retain it as a conditional inference framework. If calibrated outcomes fall outside it, investigate violated assumptions and revise the representation to include clock/readout effects or changing kinetics. If outcomes do not distinguish mechanisms, keep compatibility claims and prioritize a finite-convergence result before stronger inference. A match to the one-clock fit at tested clocks supports only those conditions.
retained_result: The proved one-clock compatibility construction and its explicit non-identification of the physical generator; the binary example shows that its homogeneous fit need not transfer across clocks.
uncertainty: No physical measurements are supplied. A cross-clock failure would test the shared-clock assumptions only for the tested setup, not refute the conditional theorem or establish arbitrary intervention behavior.
